fix_rounds.summary: Fix 2 of the ten-token audit. The shared library TokenKit.Seq is written and builds; PEPE is the pilot and has the headline 'the supply invariant holds after any finite list of transactions, whoever calls and however deep' (supply_any_transactions) with every assumption named. The other 13 tokens are NOT edited: the recipe below is what later agents apply.

kit_theorems.runner_level (every fork): Seq.processMessage_good_local (Run.lean): a sane call from a good state whose run is Clean ends good, with or without error, whatever code it runs and whatever it sends at any depth, re-entry included. Seq.processCreateMessage_good_local for creations at another address, Seq.processRunner_good_local for the runner, Seq.runFrame_keeps_local for one frame of the token under the real runner.
kit_theorems.transaction (Dencun <= fork < Glamsterda: Seq.processTransaction_good (Tx.lean): EthLib's processTransaction takes a block state where L is good to one where L is good: gas purchase, EIP-7702 authorizations, first frame, the message (call or creation), refunds, fee, end-of-transaction deletions, incorporation into the block state.
kit_theorems.any finite list: Seq.Chain + Seq.chain_good; Seq.ChainCap + Seq.chainCap_good for tokens with a gas cap.
kit_theorems.base case: Seq.ZeroBase, Seq.good_of_zero, Seq.chain_from_zero; per invariant family Seq.zeroBase_supply / zeroBase_supply2 / zeroBase_supplyMask.
kit_theorems.fork_range_honest: Message level: every fork (plus the token's own bound). Transaction level: Fork.dencun <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam. Before Dencun the end-of-transaction deletion could remove L after a SELFDESTRUCT at L; the kit avoids a per-token 'never SELFDESTRUCT' proof by tracking Unmarked, which only EIP-6780 gives.
